subject: Nanotechnology
title: Reconfigurable DNA Structures
description: A short lesson to help you apply Reconfigurable DNA Structures.

hook.text: A DNA origami box that opens when a molecular key arrives — reconfigurable structures respond to their environment.

buildup.text: Lock strands hold the structure in one state — displacement strands unlock it, triggering a shape change.

discovery.text: pH-sensitive i-motifs and G-quadruplexes enable chemical triggers — the structure folds or unfolds with acidity changes.

twist.text: Light-responsive modifications allow optical control — azobenzene in the backbone switches conformation with UV light.

climax.text: Church's lab built a DNA nanorobot barrel that opens to expose antibody payloads only near target cells.

punchline.text: DNA structures that change shape on command — programmable matter at the nanoscale.

quiz.question: How can DNA structures be made to reconfigure in response to light?
options: Light heats the DNA until it melts and reforms randomly
Azobenzene modifications in the DNA backbone change conformation when exposed to UV light
Fluorescent labels on the DNA emit light that triggers structural changes
